ops.title: Running codex (gpt-5.5) review passes from workflows — unique scratch filenames per wrapper (parallel wrappers collided and returned ONE review twice), poll to completion (10-20 min typical), codex exec --sandbox read-only -C <repo>

ops.body:
From the 2026-07-08 acct-14 fix session, running the CLAUDE.md codex review lane via sonnet-low wrappers:

**Why:** Two parallel wrappers (finder + refuter lenses) both wrote `codex_prompt.txt`/`codex_log.txt` in the shared session scratchpad; both parsed the same single codex run and returned byte-identical findings — the adversarial lens silently never ran. Separately, a wrapper returned empty findings because codex (0.142.5) was still running when the wrapper gave up: codex exec needs 10–20 min for a ~1000-line diff review.

**How to apply:**
- Every wrapper prompt must mandate UNIQUE scratch filenames (suffix by lens/run).
- Wrappers must poll the background codex pid to actual exit (bounded wait-loops, repeated) and report `codexCompleted` honestly; never accept an empty-findings return whose notes say codex was still running — re-check the log, it usually finishes minutes later.
- Working invocation: `codex exec --sandbox read-only -C <repo> "$(cat PROMPTFILE)"` with the diff + review contract in one self-contained prompt file; findings come as a final block in stdout (echoed twice — dedupe).
- Identical findings from "independent" reviewers = collision smell, not consensus; re-run the second lens.

**2026-07-10 update (codex plugin 0.10.1 wrapper still collides under concurrency).** The shipped `codex-wrapper.md` recipe uses `mktemp /tmp/codex-q-XXXXXX`/`-r-XXXXXX` (unique names), yet two concurrent workflow codex refuters (fusekit-F4 + cc-pool-P1-B1b) still collided: F4's refuter returned B1b's cc-pool review verbatim. Root cause: the sonnet-low wrapper runs write-question and read-reply as SEPARATE Bash tool calls, so the `$R` shell var is lost between calls (Bash tool doesn't persist shell state), and at read-time it globs `/tmp/codex-r-*` and picks a concurrent sibling's reply. **Fix that works: pass an EXPLICIT, unique scratchpad output path in every concurrent codex-wrapper prompt** (`.../scratchpad/codex-<stage>-r.txt`) and tell it to use those literal paths for write+`-o`+read and NEVER glob `/tmp/codex-*`. Bake this into every workflow codex stage, ESPECIALLY the whole-P1 review that runs codex ×2 in parallel (guaranteed collision otherwise). A collided review => the change was NEVER actually reviewed even if the synth returns GREEN (it just rejected the off-topic findings); re-run before trusting/tagging. See [[jj-working-copy-collision-agent-edits]] for the sibling-collision theme.
